title: Udaipur Mining & Quarrying: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Mining here is rock out of the ground, crushed, screened and trucked to construction, cement and mineral buyers. **Cash is made on volume times realisation minus royalty, diesel, explosives and haulage; the mine is the asset and the permit is the licence to earn.** The local seminar coverage is about smart mining, critical minerals and safety technology, not about tonnage or prices [1][2][3], so on unit economics the sources are silent: collect from customer the royalty rate, per-tonne realisation, diesel cost share and dispatch lead time.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the mining lease and environmental clearance, not in the crusher.** Rating commentary flags mining as highly capital-intensive [8], so capex is heavy and front-loaded while cash comes back only as dispatch happens. Working capital is short on the receivable side but heavy on stock and advance royalty; check the lease validity and any share pledge before anything else, because a rating report shows a case where the parent was an NPA and 100% shareholding was pledged to an operational creditor [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check lease tenure, clearance status and share pledge; if the lease is near renewal or shares are pledged, ask for the renewal order and a pledge release before sanction.**

## What has changed now
Peer results are strong but they are metal-price led, not Udaipur-led. **Read this as a price cycle lifting large miners, not as proof that small Udaipur quarry units are earning; the local sources say nothing about this city's tonnage, so lean on first principles and peers.**

## Who to pursue and how to grow safely
**Pursue permitted quarry operators and mineral processing units with clean royalty records, own haulage and a single end-use buyer under contract; avoid units with pledged promoter shares, parent NPA links or lease renewal pending.** Structure as a cash-flow loan against dispatch, with royalty payment proof as a condition. Take every month: royalty receipts, dispatch invoices, diesel bills and the mine's production return. **If royalty arrears appear, stop enhancement and ask for the mines department demand notice.**

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly royalty receipts (monthly): two missed or part payments -> freeze limit and inspect the mine. - Dispatch invoices versus sanctioned volume (monthly): falling volume with flat costs -> ask for buyer contracts. - Diesel and explosives spend (monthly): spend rising faster than dispatch -> reprice the loan. - Lease and clearance status (quarterly): renewal or clearance pending -> hold new sanctions.
